# MM-P1-L2-HT03-S1 Lubrication and fluids - Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3
Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P1, line P1-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L2-HT03  
This revision supersedes Rev D.

Scope
- Purpose: Define required lubricants, fluid handling, and quench timing control related to Ring Rolling heat treat furnace EQ-P1-L2-HT03.
- Applicability: Maintenance and reliability personnel responsible for routine and corrective lubrication and fluid services on EQ-P1-L2-HT03.
- Exclusions: This document does not cover process control programming, metallurgical cycle parameters, or furnace electrical systems beyond lubrication and fluids.

Background and rationale
- Proper lubrication and quench timing are critical to maintain mechanical reliability and to prevent unplanned downtime for EQ-P1-L2-HT03. Lubricant selection is driven by bearing types and the ambient oil-handling environment present on the furnace carriage and servomounts. Quench timing is monitored at the fluid delivery valve to ensure repeatable heat-treat outcomes and to protect mechanical components from thermal shock.
- The specified lubricant part number CFW-LUB-652 is selected for viscosity stability, oxidation resistance, and compatibility with seal materials used on the furnace. Field experience has shown reduced bearing wear when CFW-LUB-652 is applied per procedure.
- The quench delay maximum for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L2-HT03) is 24 seconds. This value is enforced as the maximum permissible delay between cycle completion and the start of fluid flow during quench sequences to reduce thermal gradients and avoid quench-related stress on mechanical mounting hardware.

Related documents
- SOP-P1-L2-01
- SOP-P1-L2-02
- SOP-P1-L2-03

Tools and materials
- Approved lubricant: CFW-LUB-652.
- Clean dispensing pump or sealed grease gun compatible with CFW-LUB-652.
- Lint-free wipes and solvent approved by maintenance chemistry group for seal cleaning.
- Fluid sampling bottles and labels for retention of lubricant samples.
- Personal protective equipment: oil-resistant gloves, eye protection, and shop apron.
- Lockout/tagout supplies as required by site safety procedures.
- Inspection mirror and borescope for visual inspection of hard-to-reach lubrication points.
- Torque and fastener tools are retained under separate documentation; refer to SOP-P1-L2-02 for mechanical fastening controls.

Procedure
- Preparation
  - Review current status of EQ-P1-L2-HT03 and consult SOP-P1-L2-01 for isolation requirements prior to any fluid service.
  - Place lockout/tagout on furnace motion and hydraulic sources in accordance with SOP-P1-L2-03.
  - Collect baseline condition: record current lubricant brand at sample point and visually inspect for contamination. Retain fluid sample in labeled bottle per site chemistry guidelines.
- Lubricant application
  - Clean lubrication fittings with lint-free wipe and approved solvent to remove external contamination.
  - Verify lubricant used on system is CFW-LUB-652. If previous fill differs, perform flush per site chemistry guidance before introducing CFW-LUB-652; record flush action in maintenance log.
  - Use a clean dispensing pump or sealed grease gun to deliver CFW-LUB-652 to each fitting until new, clean lubricant is observed at the return or vent point. Wipe excess and ensure no pooling occurs near electrical or hot surfaces.
  - For sealed units, inspect seals and replace if evidence of leakage or incompatibility is observed. Document seal part references in work order and reference SOP-P1-L2-02 for fastening practice when reassembling.
- Quench system verification
  - After lubricant service, verify quench valve actuation and timing sequence while system remains isolated from active heat cycles. Actuate quench control and measure delay from command to valve full open. The quench delay maximum for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L2-HT03) is 24 seconds. If measured delay exceeds 24 seconds, do not return the furnace to service; proceed to troubleshooting steps below.
- Troubleshooting (timing or contamination)
  - If quench delay exceeds specification: inspect actuator linkage, clean or replace control filters, and check for fluid contamination in control circuits. Replace filter elements per site filter change practice. Re-sample fluid and compare to baseline. Repeat timing verification.
  - If lubricant contamination is detected: isolate affected components, conduct controlled flush as per chemistry guidance, and replace lubricant with CFW-LUB-652 after confirming compatibility. Record contamination findings and corrective actions.
- Completion
  - Remove lockout/tagout and return EQ-P1-L2-HT03 to service only after successful timing verification and no evidence of leak or contamination.
  - Enter maintenance actions, parts used, and fluid sample IDs into the equipment maintenance record.

Acceptance criteria
- Lubrication: All lubrication points inspected during the activity must show fresh CFW-LUB-652 where applicable and no visible leaks at fittings or seals after reassembly.
- Quench timing: Measured delay from command to valve full open must be equal to or less than the quench delay maximum for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L2-HT03) is 24 seconds. Any measurement exceeding that value triggers follow-up troubleshooting and corrective action.
- Records: Work order must include lubricant part number used (CFW-LUB-652), sample IDs, inspection findings, and references to SOP-P1-L2-01, SOP-P1-L2-02, and SOP-P1-L2-03 as applicable.
- Sampling: Retained lubricant sample must be labeled and stored with the maintenance work order for the retention period defined by the site chemistry program.

Examples and records to keep
- Example entry in maintenance log: component serviced, lubricant CFW-LUB-652, sample bottle ID, quench timing test result, and reference to SOP-P1-L2-03 for isolation steps.
- Maintain a history file for EQ-P1-L2-HT03 documenting lubricant changeovers, contamination events, and timing anomalies with cross-reference to SOP-P1-L2-02 when mechanical replacement is performed.
- Non-conformance: If acceptance criteria are not met, create a corrective action record and tag equipment out of service until resolved.

Notes
- Coordinate any changes to lubricant specification with reliability engineering and site chemistry. Changes require revision control and cross-reference updates to SOP-P1-L2-01, SOP-P1-L2-02, and SOP-P1-L2-03.
